title: Mapa mundi del reino de las indias
title-es: Mapa mundi del reino de las indias
creator: Felipe Guamán Poma de Ayala
description-en: Colonial map of Cusco, Peru (center of the Inca empire) from a mostly Andean cosmological perspective revealing complimentary depictions of personhood. The map supposedly has a gendered reading where there is an "underworld" of gender and sexual ambivalence, which has been described as lo masculino femenino and lo femenino masculino.

title: Vocabulario en la lengua castellana y mechuacana
title-es: Vocabulario en la lengua castellana y mechuacana
creator: Maturino Gylberti
description-en: Full text here. Colonial dictionary of Michoacana written by a Spanish friar that describes the binary imposition placed on gendered bodies who supposedly display different gendered and/or presentational variations, as seen in the items "muger varonil," "muger que lo haze a otra," and "ombre de grá nariz".

title: Vocabulario en lengua misteca
creator: Francisco de Alvarado
description-en: Full text here. Colonial dictionary of the Mixteco language written by Spanish friars that demonstrates more evidence of the categorization of Indigenous people along binary gendered dimensions, as in the items "mujer casta" and "muger carnal".

title: Nota al uso del lenguaje
creator: Grupo Anarquista Pirexia
description-en: Manifesto by the Spanish anarchist group Pirexia describing their logic behind the use of gender-inclusive language in their texts, discussing the pros and cons of possible gender-inclusive alternatives, and establishing the use of the -e morpheme throughout their writings.

title: Proposición X. Género y sexo en el lenguaje escrito
title-es: Proposición X. Género y sexo en el lenguaje escrito
creator: Garazi Lara Icaza
description-en: Full text here. Master's thesis in Fine Arts that describes the use of the -x as a transfeminist artistic proposal to undermine the rigidity of the gender binary.
